clue.text: Returning chic garment not hard? That's convenient for so-called gentleman

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the letters before it are read from right to left

parts.note: chic and smart both mean stylish

indicators.note: the garment is wanted without the following letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a shirt is a garment
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard; it is removed
handy means conveniently close or useful

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a stylish garment that turned out soft, a convenience for a supposed gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both chic and the shortened garment together, so the garment's letters end up first. Sterne's novel is The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne's comic novel names its narrator a gentleman in its full title, so he is literally a gentleman by title.

clue.text: Conveyance of paintings put up on display in the community

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

indicators.note: the display word sits inside the community word, enclosed by it

parts.note: a nation is a whole community of people
to sport something is to display it, as sporting a tie

explanation.surface: A gallery arranges for its paintings to be moved and hung for public viewing in the town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, put up means read from the bottom. The display word goes in just after the first letter of the community word.
explanation.definitionFit: Transportation is the act or means of carrying people and goods, the same as conveyance.

clue.text: Persuaded elected leader to meet Democrat

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
Il Duce, Italian for leader, was Mussolini's title
D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: Someone talked a newly elected leader into sitting down with a Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade or prevail upon them to act, so persuaded matches.

clue.text: In French class you support pupil

parts.note: tu is the French word for you, as taught in a French lesson
a tee supports a golf ball before it is struck

explanation.surface: A teacher in a French lesson tells the class to help a struggling pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase about the French class is just a way of asking for the French for you.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is someone being taught by a tutor, which makes them a pupil or student.

clue.text: Here planes fly in twos, nose to tail, needing skilful pilot

indicators.note: moving the nose to the tail sends the first letter to the end of the word

parts.note: things in twos come in pairs
an ace is an expert fighter pilot

explanation.surface: Aircraft flying in formation, two by two and close behind each other, need an expert flyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose to tail' sounds like planes queueing, but it moves the P of PAIRS to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the region of sky above a territory, the place where aircraft travel.

clue.text: Position adopted by sacristan ceremoniously

indicators.note: the answer is taken in and held by the following words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A church official solemnly takes up his place during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: A sacristan is the church officer who looks after vestments and sacred vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a posture or a stated attitude, both senses of a position taken.

clue.text: Name of a companion wearing blue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the companion is worn by the colour word, so it sits inside it like clothing round a body

parts.note: blue jokes are risqué or ribald
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: The name of a friend who is dressed in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue here means smutty, not the colour; the Companion of Honour is a British order whose holders put CH after their names.
explanation.definitionFit: Archibald is a man's given name, so it is an example of a name in general.

clue.text: Injured old man's kept out of game unfortunately

indicators.note: the father figure has kept something, holding it within himself

parts.note: old man is slang for father

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is a mess, so the letters land in a disordered form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly man, hurt, has to sit out a match, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: DAD holds a rearranged GAME, giving DA-MAGE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something injured has been harmed or hurt, which is what damaged describes.

clue.text: Period in some schools to study Latin and yet play

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn

indicators.note: letters allowed to play move freely about and settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some schools set aside a stretch of time to learn Latin and still leave room for play.
explanation.walkthrough: A continental day is a school timetable that starts early and ends in the early afternoon, as in much of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a school schedule used by certain schools, so it is a period of the school day.

clue.text: A setback for top staff at university, wanting new technology installed in lecture theatres

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so the technology goes within the other letters
something set back is turned round, so the next few words are read right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or top, with the 1 read as I
a rod is a staff or stick
U is the abbreviation for university
IT, information technology, is the modern technology

explanation.surface: Senior university staff suffer a blow, needing modern technology fitted in their lecture halls.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then AI, ROD and U read backwards as UDORIA; IT goes inside after AUD. A1 standing for top is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria is the Latin plural of auditorium, a hall where an audience sits for lectures or performances.

clue.text: Part in movie failed to materialise?

wordplay.note: something that failed to materialise came to nothing: CAME plus O, the nothing

explanation.surface: An actor's film role disappeared before it appeared on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'failed to materialise' as 'came to nothing', then write nothing as the letter O after CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance by a well-known actor, a small role in a film.

clue.text: S American capital, one not included in exotic cruise

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order
one being not included means it is left out of the following letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one; it is removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South American capital city is left off the itinerary of a luxury cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, a country in South America.

clue.text: Criticising film sovereign's attending

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
a king is a sovereign
someone attending a party is at it

explanation.surface: Reviewers pan a film because the monarch turns up at its premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: Picking at someone is nagging or finding fault with them in small ways, a form of criticising.

clue.text: Arsenal's men taking ball round front of net

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: the ball goes round the following letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of net

explanation.surface: Arsenal footballers carry the ball forward round the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, but here it is the store of weapons; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means military weapons and ammunition collectively, which is what an arsenal holds or comprises.

clue.text: A quiet place in church to conceal a gadget

indicators.note: concealing something means hiding it inside, so the last letter goes within

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
taken as written
CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secluded spot in a church is used to hide something, a device of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place in church' reads as one spot, but place, in and church are three separate pieces, and the final a hides inside the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or piece of equipment for a particular task, much like a gadget.

clue.text: Someone to look after Churchill's bunker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a keeper or guardian in charge of something
second meaning, read as two words: the underground den from which Churchill ran the war

explanation.surface: Who will keep an eye on Churchill's underground headquarters?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: split the answer as WAR DEN, a fair name for the Cabinet War Rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is an official responsible for supervising a place or people, such as a park or hostel.

clue.text: Teacher's career literally flawed?

parts.note: pupils call a female teacher Miss; the 's joins her to what follows
to career is to rush headlong, to pelt along

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a teacher's professional life has been mistaken all along.
explanation.walkthrough: Career looks like a noun about a job, but it is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally here means letter by letter, so a word flawed in its letters has been wrongly spelt.

clue.text: Journeys wearily in carriages, covering miles

indicators.note: the carriages cover the following letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: traps are light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriages
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Someone travels tiredly in horse-drawn vehicles that cover many miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In carriages' tempts you to ride, but the trudging is on foot; M goes inside TRAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily and wearily over a long distance, which is journeying wearily.

clue.text: Charge read out aloud as a rule

indicators.note: reading words out loud means we judge them by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: In court, accusations are formally read out as standard practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' poses as 'usually', but it is a plus a period of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to bring them before a court to answer a criminal charge, so to charge them formally.

clue.text: Chill breeze coming from the north

parts.note: a breeze is a light wind
something coming from the north, the top of the map, is heading down

explanation.surface: A cold wind is blowing in from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Chill looks like the cold of the north wind, but it is the slang verb for relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind down is to relax gradually after effort, which is what chilling out means informally.

clue.text: Unpopular job in isolated settlement

parts.note: something unpopular is out of fashion, out
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Nobody wants the posting to a remote settlement far from anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small remote settlement or station far from the main centre of population.

clue.text: Jack and mates tossed this overboard?

definitions.text: Jack and mates tossed this overboard?

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: things tossed are thrown about, so these letters land jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor and his shipmates hurled this into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: jack is also a sailor, and his mates are the crew who threw the goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo or equipment deliberately thrown off a ship to lighten it, exactly what sailors would toss.

clue.text: Being late, crewman eats only first bit of supper

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, a member of a ship's crew
dines is eats a meal

indicators.note: keeping just the first bit of a word means taking its opening letter alone

parts.note: the first letter of supper

explanation.surface: A sailor who arrives late gets only a mouthful of the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is the quality or fact of being slow or late, a noun matching being late.

clue.text: President's killer heartlessly confronts a South African leader

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the name is taken out

parts.note: John Wilkes Booth assassinated President Lincoln
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel assassin squares up to a leader from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTH loses its central O, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Botha and P W Botha were both South African prime ministers, so either fits as a leader there.

clue.text: Violently push boat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shove roughly, as barging past someone
second meaning: a flat-bottomed cargo vessel

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an order to shove a boat off, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for shoving rudely through and a noun for a long flat canal or river vessel.

clue.text: Stars on location in Brazil given accommodation

indicators.note: a guest given accommodation is housed inside, so the city sits within the other word

parts.note: taken as written
Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil

explanation.surface: Celebrities filming in Brazil are put up in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars suggests celebrities on a shoot, but it is the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is a prominent constellation, a named group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Wanting to sleep around, mostly without clothes? That's offensive to some

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sleepy word goes around the clothes
turned around, the sleepy word is read from its end back to its start
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: someone drowsy wants to sleep
wear means clothing, as in evening wear

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to sleep around and go about naked: some find that shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep around' looks like promiscuity, but around is the reversal signal, and without has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word is a rude or blasphemous term that causes offence to some listeners.

clue.text: Colonist out east settles in with determination, sometimes

indicators.note: the colonist settles inside the following word, becoming enclosed by it

parts.note: doing something intently is doing it with resolve

indicators.note: putting the compass letter out means removing it from the colonist

parts.note: termites live in large colonies
E is the compass abbreviation for east; it is removed

explanation.surface: A settler heading east sometimes puts down roots with real resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonist looks like a human settler but is an insect that lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermittently means at irregular intervals, now and then, which is to say sometimes.
